titel: Hotel near De Maasduinen National Park | Hotel Asteria Venray
omschrijving: Stay an 18-minute drive from De Maasduinen National Park. Walk across heath and river dunes by the Reindersmeer and end the day with wellness and dinner at Hotel Asteria.
hero-sub: The longest belt of river dunes in the Netherlands, an 18-minute drive from your hotel room in Venray.
hero-alt: A sandy path across the heath in the evening light in De Maasduinen National Park
t4-waarde: De Sluis car park, with charging point
t5-waarde: On a lead, two off-lead areas
v1-p1: From Hotel Asteria it is an 18-minute drive to the visitor centre of De Maasduinen National Park in Well. The park lies on the east bank of the Maas, between the river and the German border. This is the longest belt of river dunes in the Netherlands: sand blown out of the Maas valley by the wind during the last ice age.
v1-p2: The result is a varied landscape of more than 4,000 hectares of heath, drift sand, woodland and fens. On Landgoed de Hamert there are parabolic dunes, horseshoe-shaped sand ridges up to 25 metres high. The area has been a national park since 1996 and has been called De Maasduinen since 1998.
v1-alt: A winding sandy path across the heath with scattered pines in De Maasduinen
v2-p1: The visitor centre stands on the lock between the Reindersmeer and the Leukermeer. The Reindersmeer is not a natural lake: it covers 130 hectares and was created by sand extraction on the Bergerheide. Today it is the heart of the park, with water on one side and heath on the other.
v2-p2: The centre has leaflets with walking and cycling routes. Across the park, 17 walking routes are waymarked with coloured posts, and the Pieterpad long-distance trail also runs through it. There are four semi-paved paths for wheelchairs and pushchairs.
v2-alt: The Reindersmeer in De Maasduinen National Park, with a birch and heather on the shore
v3-p1: The park's logo is a crane, which flies over the area in spring and autumn. Other residents include the beaver, the nightjar, the sand lizard and the smooth snake. The marsh gentian grows along the fens. If you walk quietly and take your time, you will see the most. Afterwards, have a coffee at Bosbrasserie In de Sluis, with a terrace above the water.
v3-alt: Sandy path beside a fen on the edge of the Bergerbos in De Maasduinen
tip: Start at the visitor centre in Well. That is where the route leaflets are, and afterwards you can have a coffee above the Reindersmeer. Wear shoes that can cope with loose sand. And if you want to use the sauna afterwards: on weekdays our wellness area opens at 4 pm, so feel free to walk until mid-afternoon.
g1-tekst: The visitor centre stands on the lock by the Reindersmeer, with route leaflets and a brasserie.
g1-alt: Wooden sculpture by Roel van Wijlick by the Reindersmeer
g2-tekst: Waymarked with coloured posts. Four semi-paved paths are suitable for wheelchairs and pushchairs.
g2-alt: Sandy path with a bench on the Bergerheide by the Eendenmeer
g3-tekst: De Sluis car park is next to the visitor centre and has a charging point. When it is busy there is an overflow car park.
g3-alt: Wooden lookout tower on the parabolic dune in the Bergerbos near Afferden
g4-tekst: Dogs must be kept on a lead. There are off-lead areas at the Bergerbos and the Eendenmeer.
g4-alt: Highland cattle grazing on the heath beneath the pines in De Maasduinen National Park
dag-kop: How to make a day of it
dag-sub: A hearty breakfast, a day outdoors in De Maasduinen, then warming up in the sauna and sitting down to dinner.
m1-tekst: The breakfast buffet is served from 7 am to 10 am on weekdays and from 8 am to 10.30 am at weekends. Then it is an 18-minute drive to Well.
m2-tekst: Pick up a route leaflet at the visitor centre and walk across heath and dunes along the Reindersmeer. You can have lunch at the brasserie on the lock.
m2-alt: Bare tree at the edge of a fen in De Maasduinen
m3-tekst: After a day outdoors the sauna is at its best. The wellness area is open from 4 pm to 10 pm Monday to Thursday and from 12 noon to 10 pm Friday to Sunday. Tuesday is swimwear day.
m4-tekst: The fresh air gives you an appetite. In the hotel brasserie you can have dinner until 9.30 pm.
kamers-sub: Then you can start a second route well rested the next morning. Choose your room; you will see the price for your dates straight away when you book.
kaart-regel: The visitor centre lies north-east of Venray, on the other side of the Maas. The driving route crosses the bridge, no ferry needed.
kaart-naam: Bezoekerscentrum De Maasduinen, Bosserheide 3e, 5855 EA Well
kaart-alt: Map of North Limburg with Hotel Asteria in Venray, the De Maasduinen visitor centre and three other days out
f1-v: How far is De Maasduinen National Park from Hotel Asteria?
f1-a: It is 17.2 kilometres to the visitor centre in Well, about 18 minutes by car. By bike it is 14.7 kilometres, around 55 minutes; that route crosses the Maas on the bicycle ferry between Vierlingsbeek and Bergen. You can hire bikes and e-bikes at our reception.
f2-v: Where is the best place to start walking?
f2-a: At the visitor centre on the Bosserheide in Well, on the lock between the Reindersmeer and the Leukermeer. That is where the route leaflets are, and you park at De Sluis car park. Another starting point is Jachthut Op den Hamer in Wellerlooi, for walks across Landgoed de Hamert.
f3-v: Can I bring my dog to De Maasduinen?
f3-a: Yes. In general, dogs must be kept on a lead in the park. There are off-lead areas at the Bergerbos in Afferden and at the Eendenmeer in Nieuw-Bergen. Check the signs on site.
f4-v: Is the park suitable for wheelchairs or pushchairs?
f4-a: The park has four semi-paved paths. Landgoed de Hamert also has a wheelchair path. Ask at the visitor centre which route is easiest to use at the time.
f5-v: Can I get something to eat or drink in De Maasduinen?
f5-a: Yes, Bosbrasserie In de Sluis is at the visitor centre, with a terrace above the Reindersmeer. Opening hours vary by season; check the brasserie website for details. For dinner you are welcome in the hotel brasserie until 9.30 pm.
f6-v: Can I still use the wellness area at the hotel after a walk?
f6-a: Yes. The wellness area is open from 4 pm to 10 pm Monday to Thursday and from 12 noon to 10 pm Friday to Sunday. Tuesday is swimwear day.

arcen.desc: More than fifteen gardens surround a 17th-century castle, from a rosarium and an Oriental water garden to the Casa Verde tropical glasshouse. The Hertog Jan Brewery is in the same village, so you can easily make a whole day of it. The gardens are closed in winter.
